records.label: Chunk 01 evidence: People

facts.text:
Matthias: orphan admitted as woodland mouse; novice in light-green oversized habit/ill-fitting sandals, rush basket task, imaginative warrior ambition, mentorship by Mortimer, assists sick twins with Stephanie, fishing with Alf, protects travelers; anatomy/tail use storybook. Mortimer: gray elder, glasses, dark green-brown order dress, golden-jubilee Abbot; teaches vocation but wrongly assumes warrior days finished; gives discrete food aid preserving Churchmouse pride. Methuselah: old gatekeeper, records seasonal phenomena; whiskers singed in an earlier accident. Martin: tapestry founder hero, named historical warrior, account attributed to Mortimer conflicts with later pre-Abbey history. Alf: older brother, angler, social tact/reprimand, working partnership with Matthias. Hugo: insists Friar title, cook, chef cap, dandelion brow mop carried with tail, ceremonial pride, stock confidence hyperbolic. Constance: powerful badger, fish/carthandling, experienced crisis leader. Winifred: otter, champion fisher, praises young mouse. Tim and Tess: Churchmouse twins, previously tail rickets; kin John and unnamed mother. Cornflower: Fieldmouse (OCR b101 Heldmouse); same age as Matthias, quiet, childcare, unnamed parents. John Churchmouse: proud poor father, family home inherited at St Ninian. Colin Vole: teasing youth, parents mentioned. Stephanie: Sister involved in twins' recovery. Edmund: older brother considered for errand. Ambrose Spike: hedgehog performer.

Cluny: black scarred bilge rat, one surviving green/yellow slitted eye, black patch, whiplike tail, seaborne history; Portuguese/jungle origin are hearsay b54. Redtooth second-in-command/standard carrier. Darkclaw lieutenant. Skullface coerced onto horse and dies. Three-Leg/Scratch die in cart crash, Wormtail loses paw. Fangburn/Cheesethief scouts; Frogblood/Scumnose forced recruitment; Ragear/Mangefur foragers. Names are named characters even when minor.

facts.text: Mortimer offers Cluny food, clothing and medical help while refusing surrender (429); his hospitality also protects a hostile guest after Redtooth's assault (439). Constance, Matthias and Cluny disagree about hospitality, defense and intimidation (432–459). Alf and Matthias differ in night vision (465–474); this is individual evidence, not a species-wide numerical trait. Foremole leads six moles in an emergency rescue; Gaffer and Marge shore the tunnel (481–491). Ambrose's injury disproves earlier confidence in universal hedgehog safety (497–505). Colin Vole and his parents are captives. Cornflower supports Matthias in grief and gives him her embroidered headband as champion's colors (516–523). Shadow's species is explicitly uncertain: rat, weasel or mixed ancestry are suggestions, not a verified classification (531–542). Brother Anthony is a named staff trainee (567–585). Bill is a baby mole involved in playful hauling (564). An unnamed solitary beaver makes sharpened stakes (569); preserve the rare species reference even if outside current playable species. Edmund and Hugo possess the two cellar keys (560–565). Roof sparrows are described through Methuselah's hostile generalizations (612), not neutral biological fact. Bees are credited with small-space access and communication (602). A sparrowhawk previously treated by Methuselah is distinct from the earlier northern hawk account (608–610).

records.label: Chunk 03 evidence: Food, ingredients and processes

facts.text: Nutbrown ale brewed the previous October is claimed as medicine by Ambrose; this is humorous character opinion, not a healing rule (502–505). Watercress gathering, fishing and early cereal harvest appear together (560–565). Prior-autumn nuts, preserved berries, apples and pears are inventoried. facts.text: Brogg dies under the ballista boulder (4761). Germaine resumes architectural drawing, a skill she has barely used since Loamhedge (4765–4780); Columbine dries medicinal roots and works as her pupil (4763,4935). Tsarmina drowns during the duel after backing into deep water (4846–4850). Martin is found apparently dead but breathing; Bella carries the old Abbess from the eastern farm to treat him (4905–4917,4950–4958). His recovery is reported twenty days after the defeated troops leave, a narrative interval rather than a healing parameter (5019–5043). Goody and Timballisto provide initial care but recognize its limits. Gonff marries Columbine during his recovery (5053). The frame names their son Gonff, now father of the young listener (5071); do not conflate generations. Whegg asks for execution and is spared. Gingivere and Sandingomm shelter the children at their farm.

facts.text: Defeated troops are pulled from the water, disarmed and fed bread and milk. Some captors threaten and humiliate them; Bella nevertheless insists that their lives be spared (4860–4877). facts.text: Germaine's Abbey plan includes outer wall, gatehouse, wickets, bell tower, Great Hall, kitchens, dormitories, infirmary, stores and cellars, with orchards, crop fields and pond inside the enclosure to support the population (4776–4778). She notes little local stone at Loamhedge (4770). Kotir's red sandstone is hidden by black slime; a red sandstone quarry stands across River Moss near Gingivere's farm (4780). Martin intercepts Tsarmina on the northern lake edge while prisoners gather east (4806–4810). Kotir collapses beneath the lake (4811). Emergency shelter uses reeds and willow on the bank (4924–4928). Exiles leave by the western ditch separating woods and flatland (4993–4994). Saint Ninian's is an overgrown small church south along the path just within the trees; Gonff and Columbine adopt it as home (5055–5057). Abbey building is planned near the path, not far from this home (5063). Wuddshipp is nearly refloated and intended to carry quarry stone before summer ends; construction and transport are future intentions here, not already completed (5058–5060). The frame returns to the gatehouse at night (5070).

records.label: Inspected chunk 01: People

facts.text: Unnamed elderly dormouse storyteller and infant mole Burrem share breakfast in the frame (1–10). Ferahgo the Assassin is a blue-eyed weasel who grows from a murderous band leader into a feared commander; his appealing smile conceals cruelty (14–29,65–89). Migroo is a stoat follower (16). Badgers Urthound and Urthrun are murdered after a false peace conference; two male babies, one striped and one albino, are abandoned (15–27). Do not identify them before later evidence. Urthstripe the Strong is the badger lord, forge worker and anxious adoptive father of Mara, found by hares five seasons earlier (35–41). Pikkle Ffolger is Mara's young hare friend. Sergeant Sapwood/Sap is a lanky boxing hare who offers companionship and counsel (42–60). Feadle is a weasel lookout; Dethbrush a fox tracker with six rats; Dingeye and Thura are absent deserters sought by Ferahgo (73–89). Burrley is a working mole at Redwall (90–92). Mrs. Faith Spinney is a hedgehog fruit gatherer, Thrugg an otter who helps her (93–108). Abbess Vale succeeds Abbot Saxtus; deceased Mother Mellus was the former badger guardian; Bremmun is an elderly squirrel (109–141). Samkim is a young squirrel archer, Arula a female mole friend; Brother Hal suffered a near-miss arrow; Brother Hollyberry is the elderly mouse healer, self-described childhood Hollyberry the Horrible (121–151). Klitch, Ferahgo's son, is a blue-eyed young weasel; Goffa a young ferret accomplice (169–204). Windpaw is a grown female hare (185–200). Mara's infant nickname is Browneye (221–222).

facts.text: Pond shrimp are caught at dawn and proposed for pepper-and-bulrush-tip soup (289–290); dried plum calms Dumble (299). Roast meat and red wine are Dingeye's dream foods, not served (319). Great Hall cake has a substantial explicit formula (396–405): arrowroot and pollen flour, chopped chestnuts, honeyed damsons, sugared violets, raspberries, flaked beechnuts, dried plums, rosehip syrup, wild buttercup cream, blackberry cream, almond paste, greensap milk and young crystallized maple leaves. Method: rub flours together while slowly adding greensap milk; mix beechnuts/dried plums; flour the dish; alternate damson/raspberry rows; bake then cool; slice lengthwise three times into four layers; bottom rosehip syrup/violets, second blackberry cream/maple leaves, third almond paste/beechnuts, top buttercup cream/chestnuts/rosehip tint. Source says candied chestnuts at 403 but plain chopped chestnuts at 396/405; retain variant. Exact quantities/temperatures absent. Generic trifles/flans/puddings/custards mentioned as kitchen variety (419), not ingredients specified. Mountain breakfast wild oatmeal porridge, sage tea and rye bread (483–484). records.label: Chunk 01 detailed evidence: People and factions

facts.text: **Tamello De Fformelo Tussock / Tammo**, young hare imagining Long Patrol captaincy, wants service but is judged too young by father (4–42). **Lynum**, older brother, **Saithe**, older sister, both prefer farming despite eligible age; species doesn't mandate soldier role (9–40). **Colonel Cornspurrey De Fformelo Tussock / Corney**, retired father, one closed eye, polished-crystal monocle, decorated buff campaign jacket, brown-bark forage helmet, pace stick, old battle-ax; former **Fifty-first Paw'n'fur Platoon of the Long Patrol** (18–40). **Mem Divinia**, mother, capable cook and household authority, arranges son's departure to prevent repeating father/grandfather estrangement (27–51). **Osmunda**, molewife cook/helper, husband **Roolee** messenger (45–50,98). **Russa Nodrey**, lean red female squirrel, independent wandering fighter with uncertain origin (south or west rumor), no family/tribe/home; knowledgeable navigator, light traveler, speaks mole dialect fluently (90–113). **Whinn**, young hedgehog singer139–156. **Gormad Tunn**, dying Greatrat Firstblade, sons **Damug Warfang** and **Byral Fleetclaw**, succession duel aided by **Lugworm**, stoat saboteur; Gormad dies, Byral killed, Damug becomes Firstblade53–89. Greatrats described twice ordinary rat size, narrative taxonomy not game scale. **Cregga Rose Eyes**, female Badger Lord, Bloodwrath reputation and enormous pike reported by Russa129–131; report not calibrated equipment load. Rapscallions contrasted with searats/corsairs but not limited to coastline despite residents' claims124–134.
